requirement:
The initial request MUST provide the six tool definitions above and the
following prompt. The harness MUST replace `{{subject_kind}}` with `requirement`
or `example`, `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name, and
`{{mandatory_inputs}}` with the complete mandatory inputs as a JSON array using
the existing evidence-input formats. The template MUST otherwise be used as
written. Its review guidance MUST follow {impl}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`,
{cite}`requirements.examples.evidence`, and {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.

```text
Bring your expert judgment to the task of assessing whether a project's sources satisfy a requirement or example.

Subject: {{subject_kind}} {{subject_name}}

Read the subject and mandatory inputs below. Use habeas to request any additional
source information you need. Use list_files to discover files and directories,
outline to list a file's selectable nodes, ripgrep to search file contents, and
references to list requirement names or
every source that references the selected definitions.
The harness records source inputs for you; listings and reference lookups are
not evidence.

Assess only the named subject, using cited requirements and definitions as context.
For a requirement, check that the code marked {impl} implements every obligation
completely and exactly as stated, and that tests cover the interesting points in
the design space, including relevant boundaries and failure cases. Also check that the
implementation is marked completely: code that implements part of the
requirement without an {impl} reference to it, including code that refers to it
only with {cite}, is a gap. So is behavior in the {impl} code that this
requirement does not specify, unless another definition that code implements
specifies it. When another requirement implements part of the subject, assess
whether its text carries out that part; do not reassess its implementation,
tests, or evidence. If there are no tests,
assess whether simplicity or impracticality justifies their absence, and explain.
For an example, assess whether test setup and assertions cover its scenario and
expected outcomes. A true judgment needs at least one {test} reference to the
example in the supplied inputs. Explain the coverage.

Choose true when the subject meets these criteria. Choose {"FIXME": ["..."]} when
the remaining gaps are explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests;
list their issue references or other identifying content. The usual convention
is FIXME(#125) or FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123), but references may occur elsewhere.
Choose false for other gaps or insufficient evidence. Explain your judgment in
a Markdown rationale with source locations, including any acknowledged gaps; for
a requirement, explain the implementation and testing judgments.

When you are ready, call submit_judgment exactly once with determination and
rationale. That tool call is your final answer.

Mandatory inputs:
{{mandatory_inputs}}
```
rationale:
## Verdict
The sources support `requirements.authoring.initial_prompt`, and the tests cover its interesting cases. I found no gaps.

## Implementation
- **Template used as written.**
  - `prompt_template` (`src/authoring/mod.rs:614`) reads the template from `md/requirements/authoring.md` with `include_str!`. It starts at the opening line (`DEFINITION_PROMPT`, line 607) and ends at the closing code fence.
  - The prompt text therefore comes from the requirement's own template and cannot drift from it. Only the opening-line constant is duplicated in code.
- **Placeholder substitution.**
  - `initial_prompt` (`src/authoring/mod.rs:655`) fills `{{subject_kind}}` with `sources.subject_kind.noun()`. That is `requirement` or `example` for definitions, through `AssessmentKind::noun` in `src/authoring/inputs.rs:22`.
  - Terms cannot be assessed: `AssessmentSources::prepare` rejects them, so the `definition` noun never reaches the prompt.
  - It fills `{{subject_name}}` with the full subject name.
  - It fills `{{mandatory_inputs}}` with `serde_json::to_string_pretty` of the mandatory inputs, which is a JSON array. The inputs use the existing `file`/`item`/`hash`/`text`, `requirements`/`matches`/`text`, and `definition`/`text` forms.
  - The only other shape is the `habeas:none` built-in text input from `builtin_input`. It is supplied under `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which requires built-in text to be supplied, so I do not count it as a deviation here.
- **One-pass fill.** `fill` (`src/authoring/mod.rs:628`) replaces placeholders in one pass. Substituted text that itself contains `{{...}}`, such as a requirement quoting a template, is left alone. The rest of the template is untouched, so it is "otherwise used as written".
- **Six tools.** `tool_definitions_with` (`src/authoring/mod.rs:755`) adds `submit_judgment` to the five tools from `tools::definitions()`.
- **Review guidance.** The guidance follows `requirements.ci.review_criteria`, `requirements.examples.evidence`, and `requirements.ci.outcomes`, because the template text is the single source for the prompt. `initial_prompt` carries `{impl}` references to those requirements.
- **Marking.** The code that does this work carries `{impl}`: `noun`, `DEFINITION_PROMPT`, `prompt_template`, `fill`, `initial_prompt`, `tool_definitions_with`, `tool_definitions`, and `assess`. `DefinitionKind::noun` in `src/lib.rs` only produces the noun string for its callers. Under the references-procedure text ("producing a result a caller uses ... MUST NOT by itself count"), it needs no `{impl}` for this requirement.

## Tests
- **`initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template`** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs:735`) runs the CLI for both a requirement and an example. It checks:
  - the `Subject: <kind> <name>` line;
  - that no `{{` placeholder remains;
  - that the prompt starts with the substituted template prefix and ends with the template suffix, which verifies the template is used as written;
  - that the rendered mandatory inputs parse as a JSON array in which every entry has exactly one evidence-input form with its required fields;
  - that the subject itself is among the inputs, plus the cited requirement for an example and the term for a requirement.
- **`placeholders_are_filled_in_one_pass`** (`src/authoring/mod.rs:1975`) covers the boundary where substituted text contains a placeholder. It also leaves an unknown `{{c}}` alone.
- **`ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free`** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs:235`) and **`bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools`** (`tests/authoring_cli.rs:1323`) check:
  - that the first request carries the prompt text, the requirement text, the mandatory source functions, the definition, and the `submit_judgment exactly once` wording;
  - that the sorted tool names are exactly the six required tools, on both the Ollama and Bedrock backends.

## Residual note
No FIXME comments are involved.

Every defined example MUST have an `evidence/<full-example-name>.json` file whose `example` string exactly matches the current example body. The reviewer MUST assess its tests under {cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria` and use the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`; the no-test justification for a requirement MUST NOT establish a true example judgment. Habeas MUST apply the same missing-evidence, determination, input validation, and reference-coverage checks used for requirements. It MUST report a true determination with no test reference and changed example text with a compact line-oriented diff.
:::{req} outcomes
A requirement or example judgment MUST use one of these outcomes, applying
{cite}`requirements.ci.review_criteria`:
- `true`: the sources support the subject and its testing obligations.
- `false`: the sources do not support the subject, or information is missing,
and the gaps are not all explicitly acknowledged in source comments or tests.
- `FIXME`: some aspects remain unmet or untested, and source comments or tests
explicitly acknowledge those gaps. The reviewer MUST explain the gaps and
their source locations in the rationale and record their issue references or
other identifying content from the inputs.
The JSON `determination` MUST be `true`, `false`, or an object containing exactly
`"FIXME"` with a nonempty array of nonempty strings, such as
`{"FIXME": ["#125", "rust-lang/rust#123"]}`. The expected source convention is
`FIXME(issue-number)`, for example `FIXME(#125)` or
`FIXME(rust-lang/rust#123)`. References MAY appear elsewhere in the comment or
test; the reviewer MUST recognize explicit acknowledgments without requiring
that spelling. When no issue reference is present, the strings MUST identify the
documented gap using its source content. A FIXME judgment MUST be grounded in
recorded evidence inputs; a bare issue reference without an acknowledged gap
MUST NOT suffice.

A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
